Public domain: every person whose words are in this text died in 1925 or earlier, so the term has ended under the law of every country, whichever one first published it.

People: Thomas Carlyle (author, Wikidata Q151403), died 1881; Jean Paul (author, Wikidata Q77079), died 1825; Johann Karl August Musäus (author, Wikidata Q213974), died 1787; Ludwig Tieck (author, Wikidata Q57239), died 1853. They are every person Project Gutenberg's catalog lists for the book ("Carlyle, Thomas, 1795-1881; Jean Paul, 1763-1825; Musäus, Johann Karl August, 1735-1787; Tieck, Ludwig, 1773-1853") and every person the printed edition's opening pages credit; each death year is Wikidata's.

Printed edition: Translations From The German Vol-iii, 1827, the Internet Archive scan https://archive.org/details/in.ernet.dli.2015.175471. Three passages of the Gutenberg text have 92%, 94%, 87% of their four-word runs in the scan's text. The scan does not show the credit of Jean Paul, Johann Karl August Musäus, whom the catalog lists; the passages show the scan holds this text.
